original_test_intent: Verify the Processor Manufacturer string for every expected SMBIOS Type 4 record matches the approved CPU vendor mapping, with explicit handling of unpopulated sockets, and remains stable after reboot.
original_method: Capture all Type 4 records, bind each by socket designation/handle/population Status, compare raw Manufacturer strings under an approved vendor-alias policy and cross-check populated sockets against OS/CPUID vendor identity without substituting it for the SMBIOS field, reboot and repeat.
manual_activity: A user approves the vendor map, alias policy and reboot plan. Complete Type 4 collection and comparison are software-controlled.
required_inputs: Approved SMBIOS Manufacturer string or alias set per populated socket
Expected handling for unpopulated Type 4 records
Validated dmidecode/transport and approved reboot/OOB plan
safety_requirements: Read SMBIOS and CPU identity only; do not alter processor or firmware state.
Preserve complete Type 4 records and raw strings; do not validate only the first grep hit.
Do not silently equate OEM/brand/reseller strings with CPU silicon vendor without an approved alias rule.
Use OS/CPUID identity as a consistency check for populated sockets, not a replacement for the SMBIOS Manufacturer field.
Stop on missing/duplicate records, mixed unexpected vendors, drift or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect all Type 4 and OS/CPUID vendor evidence, bind records by socket/status, normalize under approved aliases and compare the complete map before/after reboot.
Do not modify CPU state, invent aliases or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve expected vendor strings/aliases, socket population map and cross-check rules.
Resolve SMBIOS versus installed CPU vendor discrepancies and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The Type 4 field is relevant, but grep loses socket/population context, suppresses errors and cannot prove complete or consistent vendor mapping.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive full Type 4 output/tool/errors and OS/CPUID vendor evidence, then compare Manufacturer inside each socket-designated record under explicit alias rules.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Processor Manufacturer scope, Type 4 script and 10/10-minute values are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a complete socket/status/Manufacturer table, preserve raw SMBIOS strings, normalize only approved aliases and cross-check populated sockets against OS/CPUID vendor identity while retaining source separation across reboot.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: SMBIOS Type 4 systems, including multi-vendor-capable or partially populated platforms.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, dmidecode, BIOS, CPU and OS/CPUID tooling revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Approved CPU/platform recipe plus installed dmidecode and OS/CPUID documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds complete socket mapping, controlled alias normalization and independent populated-socket consistency evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; adds mixed/wrong-vendor and unpopulated-policy checks.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Expected vendor map and alias/population policy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Vendor string consistency does not validate CPU authenticity, model, family, stepping or functionality.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve exact aliases or an unpopulated placeholder for named sockets, but must retain raw strings and cannot normalize an unexpected vendor away.
expected_evidence: Approval, expected per-socket manufacturer/aliases/population map and tool versions
Complete pre-reboot Type 4 table plus populated-socket OS/CPUID consistency results
Complete post-reboot semantic manufacturer map comparison

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The field and persistence criterion are coherent; project vendor mapping and alias rules are readiness data.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The manufacturer string is safely readable; missing baseline and population mapping do not obscure test intent.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Replaces unscoped lines with complete socket/status vendor mapping.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Keeps multi-processor completeness and recovery while correcting capability to FULLY AUTOMATABLE.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Adds controlled vendor aliases, unpopulated-socket handling and non-substitutive OS/CPUID cross-checking.

review_improvement: Prevents one correct vendor string from hiding missing sockets, mixed unexpected vendors or placeholders and prevents overly broad normalization.
independent_technical_reasoning: After expected vendor and socket inputs are approved, all core collection/correlation/comparison steps and reboot persistence checks are automatable.
